name: Sya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Lacroix, Pierre-Francis. 1971. [Review of] Hermann Jungraithmayr, Die Ron-Sprachen. Tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien (1970). Journal de la Societe des Africanistes 41(2): 273-274. Open access athttps://www.persee.fr/doc/jafr_0037-9166_1971_num_41_2_1692_t1_0273_0000_1
tone_statements.quote: Pour chacune de ces langues le Dr Jungraithmayr présente une étude morphologique très complète, suivie d'un texte et d'un vocabulaire à deux entrées comportant 170 unités. Le lecteur en aurait donc une étude exhaustive s'il avait aussi à sa disposition les analyses phonologiques et tonologiques correspondantes qui, sauf pour le Fyer, sont absentes de cet ouvrage, et si y figurait également l'examen des questions de syntaxe, tous sujets qui doivent être abordés dans une publication ultérieure.
tone_statements.translation: For each of these languages Dr Jungraithmayr presents a very complete morphological study, followed by a text and a two-way vocabulary of 170 items. The reader would thus have an exhaustive study if he also had at his disposal the corresponding phonological and tonological analyses, which, except for Fyer, are absent from this work, and if it also included a treatment of syntax, all subjects that are to be addressed in a later publication.
tone_statements.summary: No tone system stated; records that Jungraithmayr 1970 has no tonology for Sya (only for Fyer).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2003. Why reconstructing comparative Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (Chadic Linguistics 1), 21-42. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 28: 'All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones'; p. 29: 'The falling tone in Sha and Karfa also suggests that the original tone was *la4hyal and that the tones coalesced after a long internal vowel became short.' Zero occurrences of 'stress' or 'accent' (comparative paper; scanned text from a sibling run, copied from).

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Tonalität im Tschadischen. Folia Orientalia 61.
sources.note: Mentions Sha once, as a Ron language (with Daffo, Kulere) retaining verbal Ablaut; Ron-Daffo has three tone levels; nothing on Sha stress or accent.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi & Danielle Gootjes. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Duhwa [kbz], Mindat [mmf], and Sya [scw] Languages of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-049. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 8.2 'Phonetic inventories of Duhwa, Mindat, and Sya' (pp. 16-18) gives consonant/vowel charts only; Sya data are taken from Blench's n.d. wordlist rather than collected. App. E p. 32: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sec. 3 p. 3: 'It does not appear that anyone has done further significant linguistic research on these Ron languages.' Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.quote: Pour chacune de ces langues le Dr Jungraithmayr présente une étude morphologique très complète, suivie d'un texte et d'un vocabulaire à deux entrées comportant 170 unités. Le lecteur en aurait donc une étude exhaustive s'il avait aussi à sa disposition les analyses phonologiques et tonologiques correspondantes qui, sauf pour le Fyer, sont absentes de cet ouvrage, et si y figurait également l'examen des questions de syntaxe, tous sujets qui doivent être abordés dans une publication ultérieure.
sources.note: A bibliographic tone statement only: the reviewer notes that Jungraithmayr 1970 gives full morphology, a text and a 170-item vocabulary for each language (Fyer, Bokkos, Daffo-Butura, Sya, Kulere) but that the corresponding phonological and tonological analyses are absent from the book except for Fyer, and were deferred to a later publication. It gives no tone facts for Sha itself; it establishes that the primary grammar contains no Sha tonology (confirmed by the DNB table of contents: 'Zur Tonologie' only under Fyer).
